subject: religious-studies
title: Trinity and Incarnation
welcome_lead: Enter the ecumenical councils of the patristic age where the Church hammered out its doctrines of the triune God and the incarnate Word.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on the Trinity and Incarnation: Nicaea, Chalcedon, and the contributions of Augustine and Aquinas.
final_note: You have traced how the Church confessed one God in three persons and one Christ in two natures.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Council of Nicaea (325) confessed the Son as homoousios with the Father against Arius, who held the Son was a creature. Constantinople I (381) completed trinitarian doctrine by affirming the divinity of the Holy Spirit, who 'proceeds from the Father' and is 'worshipped and glorified' with the Father and Son. The Cappadocian Fathers (Basil, the two Gregorys) gave the formula: one ousia, three hypostases.

Against Apollinarianism (Christ lacks a human mind), Nestorianism (two persons) and Eutychianism (one mixed nature), the Council of Chalcedon (451) defined Christ as 'truly God and truly man. in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation', united in one person and hypostasis.

walkthroughs.h2: Augustine and Aquinas on the Trinity
walkthroughs.body_html: Augustine, in De Trinitate, develops psychological analogies (memory, understanding, will) for the inner life of God. Aquinas, in Summa Theologiae I, QQ.27-43, distinguishes the divine persons by their relations of origin: paternity, filiation, and spiration. Both stress that the external works of the Trinity are undivided (opera ad extra sunt indivisa).

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe in three different gods.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

mcqs.q: In what year did the Council of Nicaea meet?
Arius, condemned at Nicaea (325), taught that the Son:
options: was a created being — 'there was when he was not'
had no real human body
was identical with the Father with no distinction of persons
possessed two wills, one divine and one human

mcqs.q: Docetism is the claim that Christ:
options: only appeared to be human and did not truly suffer
was merely human and not divine
had a human body but no human mind
was adopted as Son at his baptism

mcqs.q: Modalism (Sabellianism) errs, according to orthodoxy, by teaching that:
options: Father, Son and Spirit are successive roles or masks of one person, not three distinct persons
there are three separate gods
the Son is of the same substance as the Father
the Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son
